arrival_shapes.files: Data files plus a small delivery manifest written last (the landing contract).
arrival_shapes.change_files: Files whose rows carry an operation (insert, update, delete), a change sequence and a commit time.
arrival_shapes.tables: A table that someone else keeps, read by version or change feed (a shared or managed table).
arrival_shapes.events: An unbounded flow of small records, delivered at least once, possibly late or repeated.

initiators.push: A third party delivers on its own schedule (a partner drop, a vendor export).
initiators.pull_mover: The platform starts something else that delivers files (a managed copy service, a warehouse export command).
initiators.share: Nothing moves. The data is read in place from a table someone shares.

capabilities.bulk_export_to_files: The source can write a large slice to files itself (fastest, least load on the source).
capabilities.incremental_by_watermark: A reliable change-time or increasing key lets a load ask for what is new.
capabilities.log_based_changes: Changes are read from the source's own change log, with operation and sequence.
capabilities.deletes_visible: A delete shows up as an event, a flag or a separate list.
capabilities.ordered_changes: Changes carry a sequence that settles which came last.
capabilities.zero_copy_read: The data is read where it is, with nothing copied by us until we choose to.
capabilities.history_guaranteed: The provider promises how long old versions can be read.
capabilities.row_read: Rows can be read through a standard database or API interface (the universal, slowest route).

proof_levels.0: Declared. A name in a list, no code.
proof_levels.1: Code exists (a connector, a generator) but has not been run against a fake or a real source.
proof_levels.2: Run against a fake, an emulator or a local copy.
proof_levels.3: Run against a real instance for a full load, an incremental load, a delete and a schema change.
proof_levels.4: Hardened for production, with secrets, retries, a volume test, a runbook and supported versions written down.

families.name: Files in storage

questions.changes: New files appear. A file is complete only when a marker or a manifest says so.
questions.deletes: Not visible, except through a later full snapshot.
questions.order_and_repeats: Files can be resent, renamed or arrive late. The same bytes twice must change nothing.
questions.who_starts: The sender, or a copy service we start.
questions.what_arrives: Files, in whatever format the sender chose.

families.approach: Land the files untouched with a manifest, refuse a second write to a delivery, then read.
families.fallback: A listing job that copies new files and writes the manifest, when the source cannot write a manifest.
families.contract_test: Delivery names are unique, the manifest comes last, a duplicate write is refused, row counts agree.

families.name: Databases with log-based change capture

questions.changes: Read from the database's change log, with operation, sequence and commit time.
questions.order_and_repeats: Ordered by sequence. Overlap between the first full load and the first changes needs removing.
questions.who_starts: A capture tool, started by us or by the owner.
questions.what_arrives: Change files, or an event flow.

families.approach: Take a full baseline, then apply the changes by sequence. Keep deletes soft.
families.fallback: Query-based loading (F3) with a soft-delete column, or a periodic full copy compared by key.
families.contract_test: Insert, update, delete, a change that arrives late, a replayed change, a feed that silently drops rows.

families.name: Databases without a change feed (query-based)

questions.changes: Only through a change-time column or an increasing key. Without one, only a full copy works.
questions.deletes: Invisible. Needs a soft-delete column, or a full copy compared by key.
questions.order_and_repeats: A change-time column can lag or be edited, so a window overlaps and repeats are removed.

families.approach: Ask for a window by watermark, write files plus a manifest, advance the watermark only after the load.
families.fallback: A full copy compared by key to find deletes.
families.contract_test: A full load, an incremental window, a row changed inside the window twice, a missing delete.

families.name: Warehouses and lakehouses as sources

questions.changes: Same as F3, plus whatever the warehouse offers to write or share a table.
questions.deletes: Usually invisible. A shared table may expose them.
questions.order_and_repeats: The export runs on the owner's compute and can slow their reports.
questions.who_starts: A job we start that makes the warehouse write files, or a table the warehouse shares.

families.approach: Prefer the warehouse's own bulk export to files. If it can write an open table, read that (F5). Query in place only for small tables.
families.fallback: Partitioned row reads through a standard interface, written as files.
families.contract_test: The F3 table, plus a large backfill and a check that the owner's load stays within a limit.

families.name: Shared or managed tables (zero copy)

questions.changes: Table versions, or a change feed when the provider shares history.
questions.deletes: Visible in a change feed. Otherwise a full snapshot compared by key.
questions.order_and_repeats: A version is atomic. A version the provider has removed cannot be re-read.
questions.who_starts: Nothing to start. We read on our schedule.

families.approach: Read by version range, record the range and row counts as the batch, keep only the copy the dataset's policy allows.
families.fallback: A snapshot read at one version, with deletes found by key comparison.
families.contract_test: A provider that adds a column, restates rows, removes old versions, and shares a change feed or does not.

families.name: Business applications through APIs

questions.changes: A cursor or a modified-time field. Custom fields change the schema.
questions.deletes: Often a separate endpoint or a flag.
questions.order_and_repeats: Pages shift while we read. Rate limits apply.
questions.who_starts: A managed connector, or our own pager.

families.approach: Use a managed connector where one exists. Otherwise page with a cursor and write files plus a manifest.
families.fallback: Our own pager over the public interface.
families.contract_test: A page boundary that shifts, a rate limit, a custom field added, a deleted record.

families.name: Event streams

questions.deletes: A tombstone event, if the producer sends one.
questions.order_and_repeats: Ordered per partition only. Delivered at least once. Late and repeated events are normal.

families.approach: Read from a saved position into bronze, drop repeats by event id, place late events by event time.
families.fallback: A buffered export of the stream to files.
families.contract_test: A replay, an out-of-order burst, a gap, a restart from the saved position.

families.name: Documents and media

questions.order_and_repeats: The same document in several versions.
questions.who_starts: The sender, or a copy service.
questions.what_arrives: Files that need text or fields extracted.

families.approach: Land untouched, extract text or fields in a separate step, keep the link from every extracted row to its file.
families.fallback: Manual upload to a landing folder.
families.contract_test: An unreadable file, a scanned page, a changed version of a file.

products.name: SAP (S/4HANA, ECC, HANA, Business Data Cloud)
products.policy: Only routes the vendor certifies. Do not read the tables of an S/4 system directly (licence and support rules).

routes.name: Business Data Cloud Connect (zero-copy sharing)
routes.evidence: Generally available; shared through the open sharing protocol; each data product must be shared explicitly

routes.name: Export to files by the vendor's data tools
routes.constraint: Depends on the tool and its cost

routes.name: HANA as a plain database (query)
routes.constraint: Not for the tables of an S/4 system

products.name: Salesforce
products.policy: Prefer the managed connector or zero-copy sharing over our own pager.

routes.name: Lakeflow Connect managed connector
routes.evidence: Generally available on the three clouds; some products unsupported (for example B2C Commerce Cloud)

routes.name: Data Cloud zero-copy sharing and federation
routes.evidence: Offered by Databricks beside the connector

routes.name: Bulk and REST interfaces through a copy service

products.name: Oracle Database
products.policy: Prefer log-based capture. Query-based only with a trustworthy change-time column.

routes.name: Log-based capture to files or a stream
routes.constraint: Needs the owner's capture setup and licence

routes.name: Query-based incremental
routes.evidence: A connector class exists in the older framework; not wired into the platform

products.name: SQL Server and Azure SQL
products.policy: Prefer the managed connector or the engine's own change capture; query-based as the fallback.

routes.name: Copy service
routes.evidence: Pipelines generated and tested offline (24 tests); never run against a database

routes.name: Query-based incremental
routes.evidence: A connector class exists in the older framework

products.name: PostgreSQL
products.policy: Query-based today. Log-based capture needs a decision on the tool.

routes.name: Query-based reader
routes.evidence: The platform's own source adapter runs against a real local PostgreSQL, with the simulated company's tables

routes.name: Log-based capture
routes.constraint: Needs a capture tool and a replication slot

routes.name: Query-based incremental
routes.evidence: A connector class exists in the older framework

products.name: Amazon Redshift
products.policy: Often a derived copy. For ongoing loads go upstream when the upstream sources are reachable. Export for history.

routes.name: UNLOAD to files
routes.constraint: Runs on the owner's compute; needs a role on the cluster

routes.name: Write to an open table (Iceberg)
routes.evidence: Redshift can write Iceberg tables to S3 (generally available Nov 2025); append-oriented
routes.constraint: Depends on the client's version and region

products.name: Snowflake
products.policy: Prefer a table share or an export to files over row reads.

routes.name: Row reads through a standard interface

products.name: Cloud object storage (S3, ADLS, GCS)
products.policy: Land the files untouched and write the manifest.

routes.name: Azure Data Lake Storage (CSV files through the copy service)
routes.evidence: Run for real on 20 Nov 2026: 3 deliveries landed, the lander loaded 1 and skipped 2 as duplicates

products.name: SFTP and partner file drops
products.policy: Land the files untouched and write the manifest.

routes.name: Copy service or our listing job
routes.evidence: A connector class exists in the older framework

products.name: A generic REST interface
products.policy: Our pager is for the long tail. Prefer a managed connector for a named product.

routes.name: Our paged reader
routes.evidence: Runs against the simulated company's dealer interface

products.name: Event streams (Kinesis, Event Hubs, Kafka, IoT)

routes.name: Amazon Kinesis
routes.evidence: Tested on a fake AWS; the replay and out-of-order incidents are handled

routes.name: Azure Event Hubs
routes.evidence: The provider is registered; no adapter

products.name: Documents and media
products.policy: Land untouched, extract in a separate step.
